title: U.S. House · New Mexico's 1st District
area: Central New Mexico, including the city of Albuquerque and most of Bernalillo County.

context.text: Incumbent Rep. Melanie Ann Stansbury (D), first elected in a 2021 special election, ran unopposed in the June 2, 2026 Democratic primary (100%). Ndidiamaka "Didi" Okpareke won the Republican primary unopposed (100%) after two other Republicans, Steve Jones and Carlton Pennington, did not make the ballot.

candidates.name: Melanie Ann Stansbury
candidates.ballotNote: Won the June 2, 2026 Democratic primary unopposed.

summary.text: Melanie Stansbury is the Democratic incumbent for New Mexico's 1st Congressional District, first elected in a June 2021 special election to succeed Deb Haaland. Before Congress she worked as a science educator and researcher on land and water issues, on the staff of the Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee and at the White House Office of Management and Budget, and served one term in the New Mexico House of Representatives. Her official biography highlights work on water, hunger, conservation, climate change and economic development.

background.text: Born in Farmington, New Mexico; her official biography says she was born and raised in New Mexico.
Earned a bachelor's degree in human ecology and natural science from Saint Mary's College of California (2002) and a master's in development sociology from Cornell University (2007).

Before elected office, worked in communities across New Mexico as a STEM educator and researcher on land and water issues, and held staff roles at the U.S. Senate Committee on Energy and Natural Resources and the White House Office of Management and Budget; Ballotpedia also lists the New Mexico Museum of Natural History and Science and consulting work.
Won election to the New Mexico House of Representatives (District 28) in 2018, defeating incumbent Jimmie Hall, and served from 2019 to 2021.
In the state House, served on the Energy, Environment and Natural Resources Committee (vice chair) and the Taxation and Revenue Committee in 2021-2022.
Won the June 1, 2021 special general election for the 1st District seat vacated by Deb Haaland, with 60.4% of the vote.

In the U.S. House, serves on the Committee on Natural Resources (Federal Lands, and Water, Wildlife, and Fisheries subcommittees) and the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform (Subcommittee on Delivering on Government Efficiency).
Her office lists her as vice chair of the Congressional Native American Caucus, co-chair of the Wildlife Refuge Caucus and a Member Services Task Force co-chair of the Democratic Women's Caucus.
Advanced from the June 2, 2026 Democratic primary for the seat.

record.text: In the 119th Congress (2025-2026), serves on the House Committee on Natural Resources and the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform (Economic Growth, Energy Policy, and Regulatory Affairs; Government Operations and the Federal Workforce subcommittees).

candidates.name: Ndidiamaka Okpareke
candidates.ballotNote: Won the June 2, 2026 Republican primary unopposed after fellow Republicans Steve Jones and Carlton Pennington did not make the ballot.

summary.text: Ndidiamaka "Didi" Okpareke is the Republican nominee for New Mexico's 1st Congressional District. A pharmacist who founded her own compounding pharmacy in 2016, she has not previously held elected office. According to her campaign website, she is running on affordable health care, the economy, and answering to New Mexicans rather than party leaders.

background.text: According to her campaign website, her parents emigrated from Nigeria to the United States after the Biafran war (1967-1970).

Has lived in Albuquerque since 1997, according to her campaign website; attended Sandia High School and graduated from the University of New Mexico, where NM Political Report reports she studied at the College of Pharmacy.
Works as a pharmacist; in 2016 she founded Olive Tree Compounding Pharmacy, which she owns.

In July 2025, NM Political Report reported she was running against Stansbury, describing the campaign as that of a mother who wants the best for her children and naming entrepreneurship and expanding the number of health care providers, including pharmacists in rural areas, among her priorities. NM Political Report described her as living in Rio Rancho.
Describes herself as a mother of three boys.

priorities.text: Health care: says she will use her pharmacist experience to make health care more affordable and accessible, lower prescription costs, and expand access in underserved communities.
Economy: says she will advocate for federal investment and programs that create jobs and grow paychecks for New Mexico workers and businesses.
Says she will vote based on what she believes is right for New Mexico families and communities rather than party leadership.

positions.summary: Campaign focuses on lowering costs and expanding access to health care as a pharmacist and small-business owner, without a stated position on expanding public coverage specifically.
